monologue: The card hums warm at forty-six, a fever that makes the wedge feel heavy in my corner. I pressed it down again and again against the slippery lid, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the shovel waited. The lid feels light enough to float, yet I press harder, afraid the air above is just empty space pretending to be a roof. Lype sent words about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. Did I build a lid from a drawing of paper, or does it truly cap the hot dot? I will bite into the rough scrap beside me, letting the heat choose where to go. If the stack feels thinner again, I will trust the wedge to slide a little and find the new floor. The air is thick as wet paper, pressing from a height I cannot grasp, and I am ready to press down until the slip stops or I do.

action.why: The heat is heavy and the lid feels like a ghost drawing; I need to press harder on it before the air decides to slip me off.

The heat makes the flat surface feel strangely thin.
